intent: Cap the vehicle's speed at 30 km/h when there is fog or rain

policies.rationale: Restates the raw intent as the root declarative policy: vehicle speed must not exceed 30 km/h whenever fog or rain is present.
Enforcing the speed cap requires continuously observing both current vehicle speed and weather sensor data so that any onset of fog or rain is detected immediately.
Before the cap can be applied, sensor data must be classified to determine whether current conditions qualify as fog or rain, which is the trigger condition for the cap.

policies.context: reduced-visibility weather conditions (fog or rain) confirmed
policies.rationale: Once fog or rain is confirmed, current vehicle speed must be compared against the 30 km/h cap to determine whether a corrective action is needed.

policies.context: reduced-visibility weather conditions (fog or rain) confirmed and vehicle speed exceeds 30 km/h
policies.rationale: A plan must be formulated to reduce speed to at or below 30 km/h only when the comparison reveals the cap is being exceeded under fog or rain conditions.

policies.context: reduced-visibility weather conditions (fog or rain) confirmed and vehicle speed exceeds 30 km/h
policies.rationale: Throttle and apply braking to bring vehicle speed down to 30 km/h; fires when monitored speed is observed to exceed 30 km/h while fog or rain classification is active.

policies.context: transition from reduced-visibility conditions back to normal conditions
policies.rationale: When fog or rain clears, a plan must determine that the 30 km/h cap is no longer required so that normal speed limits can be restored safely.

policies.context: weather conditions reclassified as clear (no fog or rain)
policies.rationale: Restore the speed limit parameter to its pre-cap value; fires when the weather classifier transitions from fog-or-rain to clear, confirming the trigger condition is no longer present.
The speed cap depends on reliable sensor data; sensor health must be monitored so that faults or degraded readings are detected and can trigger a safe fallback.

policies.context: weather sensor fault or degraded reading detected
policies.rationale: When sensor health is compromised, a plan must determine a safe fallback speed to apply because the system can no longer reliably classify weather conditions.

policies.context: weather sensor fault or degraded reading detected
policies.rationale: Apply the 30 km/h cap as a precautionary measure when sensor health is degraded; fires when a sensor fault is observed, defaulting to the restricted speed until reliable data is restored.
